vikram: Trying to settle an argument — for client-facing SDKs that need fast fallback (browser + server) do we standardize on gRPC-web with a tiny JSON bridge at the edge, or stay REST-first and add optional streaming gRPC for high-throughput internal calls? Need to think about how quotas + per-route metrics surface in Console.
sasha: My gut is REST-first for SDK ergonomics, but we lose streaming semantics. gRPC-web gives better perf for long polling/streaming.
vikram: Right; but if we pick REST-first we need a consistent way to carry routing hints and model/version pins so the Console can show per-model latency histograms.
alex: We could add headers like `x-rw-routing` and `x-rw-model` for REST and translate to proto metadata for gRPC. Console just reads those telemetry tags.
tia: Quick note — that header approach works but it becomes messy when SDKs call internal services that rewrite headers. We should define a canonical propagation spec (3 fields max).
drew: Can we reuse existing trace/span propagation (traceparent) to also carry model pins? Feels wrong semantically but would piggyback nicely.
sasha: I don't want model pins mixed into trace ids; makes tracing tools noisy. Better to add a dedicated attribute in our telemetry ingest and require services to attach it.
opsbot: Deploy bot: Canary rollout alpha-v2 models to 10% traffic in us-west activated by rollout id `canary/alpha-v2` at 2026-03-21T16:12:03Z
vikram: For quotas, we need token-level attribution in Console (token X used model Y, cost Z). If we do gRPC only, that attribution is straightforward in the proxy; if REST, more work on the gateway to parse bodies for embeddings vs text gen.
alex: Gateway parsing sucks for performance. Alternative: require clients to set `x-rw-workload-type: embeddings|text-gen|chat` — then routing + quota can be consistent without body inspection.
tia: Agreed on workload header. But we need strong validation in SDKs and gateway to avoid bad actors spoofing headers. Signed header or token-bound claim?
drew: Token-bound claim seems more robust: token metadata includes allowed workload types and model pins. Gateway reads token and sets internal metadata. No untrusted client headers.
sasha: That increases token validation load at edge. Do we have capacity to do crypto checks at 100k rps?
vikram: We can cache token introspection results in the edge for short TTLs + fingerprinting. Also can add a fallback path: unauthenticated/legacy tokens hit REST-only route with stricter quotas.
opsbot: Incident bot: Observability alert — routing-bridge latency p95 spiked 320ms in us-east-1 at 2026-03-20T04:03:01Z (investigating) :mag:
alex: That spike reinforces we need lightweight headers, not deep body parsing. Even adding a small proto-to-json transcoder increases p95.
tia: UX ask for Console: show per-route fallback rate (percent of requests that dropped from streaming to non-streaming), plus per-token cost breakdown and rollout exposure.
drew: Also add a small drilldown: for tokens with high fallback, show recent requests + model pin history so SRE/product can decide to widen canary.
sasha: Implementation plan suggestion: 1) Define token-bound metadata schema (workload, allowed models, rollout ids) 2) Edge tokens cache + signer verification 3) Propagate internal metadata via gRPC metadata and `x-rw-*` for REST internal hop 4) Console reads ingest and shows per-token/model metrics and fallback rate.
vikram: That plan sounds good. Two unresolved tradeoffs: SDK ergonomics (REST vs gRPC-web) and edge CPU cost for token validation. I'm leaning to: default REST + optional gRPC-web for advanced SDKs; token metadata validation with aggressive caching. Thoughts?
alex: +1 for default REST, optional gRPC-web. Keep SDK onboarding simple.
tia: +1 but let's prototype token cache perf before locking.
drew: I'll run a small load test with token-introspection caching sim 150k rps and report numbers.
sasha: If test looks good, we can write a short RFC and wire Console prototype.
vikram: Cool — Drew, can you post results by EOD Friday? If perf is bad we revisit a simpler header-only fallback route for free-tier tokens.
drew: Yep, will do.
